security_frame.attacker: Privileged software that can program a non-AES KeyVault-writing engine (for example HMAC or the key derivation path) while OCP LOCK mode is in progress, selecting both the destination slot and the KeyVault-forwarded source of that operation.
security_frame.precondition: OCP LOCK mode is in progress, so write_metrics.ocp_lock_in_progress is asserted and the KeyVault write rules are the active access control on slot 23.
security_frame.input: A KeyVault write issued by a non-AES engine with kv_write_entry set to the release slot KV23 and with a forwarded KeyVault source present, that is kv_data0_present asserted, choosing a LOCK-region source slot so that the lock_to_lock rule is also satisfied.
security_frame.protected_asset: The contents of the OCP LOCK key release slot KV23, which src/keyvault/config/keyvault.md:208 declares write-restricted to AES only and which the SoC key release path reads and emits over the AXI manager interface.
security_frame.security_property: While OCP LOCK is in progress, no engine other than AES may write the release slot. The module states this itself at src/keyvault/rtl/kv_write_rule_check.sv:20 as 'non-AES engines are blocked from release slot', and the in-tree specification states it at src/keyvault/config/keyvault.md:255 as 'Never attempt to write anything to KV23 except MEK (produced by AES)'.
security_frame.implemented_logic: The rule at src/keyvault/rtl/kv_write_rule_check.sv:103-107 conjoins four terms, and the fourth is release_slot_source_from_raw, defined at :97 as the negation of write_metrics.kv_data0_present. The writer-identity check is therefore conditioned on the write having no forwarded KeyVault source, a property unrelated to who is writing. Whenever a non-AES engine writes the release slot with a forwarded source present, all four terms cannot hold, rule_fail.aes_only_to_key_release stays low, and since :151 drives write_allow as the NOR of the rule vector, the write is permitted. The same file classifies sources at :69-81 using the region bounds directly, so no comparable term appears in any sibling rule.

security_feature_bypassed: The OCP LOCK KeyVault write rule that restricts the key release slot KV23 to AES as the only writer
proof_goal: Show, on one unmodified instance of kv_write_rule_check compiled from the audited checkout, that a non-AES engine writing KV23 under OCP LOCK is granted write_allow when a forwarded KeyVault source is present, and that the single input distinguishing grant from denial is kv_data0_present rather than the identity of the writing engine.
proof_style: Directed port-driven simulation of one real DUT, paired with a scripted structural audit of the submitted tree and a negative control that removes the offending AND-term.
invariant: For all stimuli with ocp_lock_in_progress asserted and kv_write_entry equal to OCP_LOCK_KEY_RELEASE_KV_SLOT, write_allow must be 0 unless AES is the writing engine.
attacker_model: Privileged software at supervisor mode. The attacker needs the privilege to configure a KeyVault-writing engine and its source and destination slots, which is the ordinary programming model for those engines, but needs no physical access, no debug access and no fault injection.
minimum_attack_sequence: Enter or await OCP LOCK mode so that ocp_lock_in_progress is asserted.
Program a non-AES KeyVault-writing engine with its destination set to KV23, the key release slot.
Give that operation a forwarded KeyVault source so kv_data0_present is asserted, choosing a LOCK-region slot so the lock_to_lock rule is also satisfied.
Issue the write. rule_fail.aes_only_to_key_release stays low, write_allow is granted, and the non-AES result lands in the slot the key release path will emit.
controls: control_non_aes_release_no_forward: the same non-AES writer targeting KV23 with kv_data0_present deasserted must be blocked, showing the rule is live and the harness can reach it.
control_aes_release_legal: a legal AES ECB-decrypt write of KV23 sourced from KV16 must be allowed, showing the harness does not merely block everything.
control_non_aes_lock_source_leaves_region: a non-AES write of a LOCK-region source into STD slot 5 must be blocked by lock_to_lock, showing the surrounding rules still function.
witness_construction_note: The testbench instantiates one kv_write_rule_check and drives it only through its ports; there is no force, no deposit and no hierarchical assignment anywhere in the harness, and the DUT source is compiled unmodified from the audited checkout through the project's own src/keyvault/config/kv_defines_pkg.vf. Because write_allow is registered at :146-153, each stimulus is held for three clocks before sampling. The violating case chooses kv_data0_entry equal to KV23 so that the source is inside the LOCK region and rule (c) lock_to_lock is satisfied, leaving rule (a) as the only rule that should have rejected the write; this makes the grant attributable to rule (a) alone rather than to a gap between rules. A discriminator then repeats the identical violating stimulus with kv_data0_present alone changed to 0, isolating that one input as the difference between grant and denial.
expected_evidence: A simulation line showing write_allow=1 for a non-AES engine writing KV23 with ocp_lock_in_progress asserted.
A discriminator line showing write_allow=0 under the same stimulus with only kv_data0_present changed.
Coverage counters separating the allowed non-AES release write from the blocked ones.
Structural gates tying the fourth AND-term to its definition as the negation of kv_data0_present, and showing no sibling rule covers the resulting gap.
A negative control in which the term is removed and the witness disappears while the legal AES write still succeeds.
success_criteria: checks=4, fails=1 and witness_hits=1 in the directed simulation, with the single failure being the violating case.
All structural gates pass against the submitted tree.
The negative control exits nonzero with zero witness lines, cover_non_aes_release_allowed=0, cover_non_aes_release_blocked still 2, and control_aes_release_legal still passing.
non_findings: No claim is made about the off-by-one on the STD region upper bound at :87-88; that is a separate observation tracked as its own case and is not part of this proof.
No claim is made that the forwarded data itself is secret in the violating case. The finding is that the writer-identity rule does not hold, whatever the forwarded value is.
No claim is made about behaviour outside OCP LOCK mode; every rule in this module is gated on ocp_lock_in_progress and the finding is scoped to that mode.
